"Score how well this research card fits each existing programme below. Each programme lists claims about its current practice; two checkers fetched each source and marked each claim SUPPORTED, PARTIAL, UNSUPPORTED, CONTRADICTED or UNREACHABLE. Rely only on claims that at least one checker marked SUPPORTED or PARTIAL. Score each programme 1-5 on each criterion, with a reason of at most 25 words. Decide only from the text below; do not use tools.
Root question: Can molecular mapping of AAV capsid-receptor interactions on brain microvascular endothelial cells determine which AAV variants transcytose across the blood-brain barrier versus remain intracellular, and for which capsid-receptor binding signatures?
Card:
**Option 1: Exhaustive capsid–receptor complex enumeration (docking and AlphaFold-Multimer) · Exhaustive capsid–receptor complex enumeration (docking and AlphaFold-Multimer).** seed pick · compute tested: yes · plan expects: not the lever · PASS

**Question.** Does exhaustive modeling of AAV capsid–receptor complexes reveal a shared interface motif, like 3-fold-axis GPI-receptor engagement, that marks which capsids transcytose the BBB?

**What is known.** The earlier APPRAISE-AAV study used AlphaFold-Multimer, ten replicate models per matrix, to rank capsid peptides against the receptors LY6A, LY6C1 and CA4, validating one PHP.eB–LY6A pose [s_appraise]. Whether a shared 3-fold-axis GPI-engagement motif marks transcytosis-competent pairs across a whole capsid panel, or whether deeper pose sampling changes that call [s_appraise].

**Hypothesis.** Transcytosis-competent capsids engage GPI-anchored BBB receptors at the capsid 3-fold spike with a shared anchor geometry, unlike non-cognate pairs [s_appraise].

**If compute is the lever.** At 2,880 models the competent-minus-retained GPI-engagement gap reaches 0.50 or more, while at 144 models it stays below 0.25.

**If not.** The gap stays within 0.15 of its 144-model value at every depth; added poses change nothing because insert location already fixes the 3-fold site [s_cat].

**Test.** Run 72 pairs at 144, 720, 2,880 pose models on 8x A100s [s_lambda], anchored on the published PHP.eB–LY6A complex [s_appraise]; compare with the ten-model published baseline and the 144-model shallow arm against phenotype labels [s_alpl].

*Compute axis.* Capsid–receptor pose models computed per panel sweep (rigid-docking poses plus AlphaFold-Multimer seed models): 144–2,880 pose models, 3 levels. Closest prior: 10 [s_appraise_rep], beyond it.

*Restructuring.* none.

**Check first.** Rebuild the published PHP.eB peptide–LY6A complex and require its validated contacts and capsid fit before any library spend [s_appraise]. Tolerance: capsid-fragment RMSD to PDB 7WQO at most 1.5 Å (published engineered-loop RMSD is 1.36 Å) and at least 2 of the 3 named contacts (peptide Pro5', Phe6', LY6A Ala58) within 5 Å.

**Would not show.** Predicted interface geometry only, not transcytosis rates or post-binding fate; weak avidity-dependent contacts may evade prediction [s_appraise]; twelve capsids, six receptors.

*Cost.* Plans $955.84 of the $1,000 budget over 59 machine-hours, leaving $44.16. Main guess: wall minutes per AlphaFold-Multimer seed job [g], measured after $51.74 of spend; the budget is reached if it is 1.1× higher. 2 cost flags in the block.

In practice this is done with human surface-protein binding/transduction screens, SPR, and a polarized cell-barrier Transwell assay, not with exhaustive structural enumeration.\",\"practice\":[\"Scale of the discovery funnel feeding the receptor step: TRACER-NHP libraries start at ~4E7 individual capsid variants, narrowed by two in vivo macaque passages to ~1,500 variants of interest before receptor work. [SUPPORTED, SUPPORTED]\",\"Receptor identification is done experimentally with two orthogonal screens (human surface-protein binding microarray and ORFeome transduction screen), not by complex modeling. [SUPPORTED, SUPPORTED]\",\"The transcytose-versus-retain call is made in a polarized cell-barrier (MDCK Transwell) model: human ALPL expression raises VCAP-102 transcytosis >100-fold while AAV9 is unaffected. {\"programme\":2,\"name\":\"Gradinaru Lab (Caltech) / APPRAISE-AAV — receptor-directed AAV engineering and the open-source APPRAISE package\",\"step\":\"The computational step the card scales: ranking engineered capsid insertion peptides against BBB receptors by AlphaFold-Multimer pairwise competition modeling, scored with atom-counting energy plus binding-angle and pocket-depth geometry, used to classify receptor-dependent vs receptor-independent capsids and to pick candidates before in vivo selection. Today this runs at ten models per competition on single-GPU Colab sessions; the card asks whether 144–2,880 pose models per pair change the transcytosis call.\",\"practice\":[\"Standard depth of pose sampling is ten AF-Multimer models per pairwise competition (five predictions per input order, two orders), averaged into a round-robin ranking matrix. [SUPPORTED, SUPPORTED]\",\"Scale and cost of the step today: a 100-capsid HT-APPRAISE screen completed in 24 h on three parallel Colab GPU sessions, with ~0.1–1 GPU minute per peptide–receptor model and sub-second CPU scoring. [SUPPORTED, SUPPORTED]\",\"Applied to LY6A, LY6C1 and CA4, the 10-model ranking recovered validated binders but produced documented false negatives — the exact failure mode deeper pose sampling is meant to fix. [SUPPORTED, SUPPORTED]\",\"Where full complex modeling has been run (LRP6–capsid VR-VIII), the lab used only five AF-Multimer models with up to 20 recycles on a single A100, and validated poses experimentally and on macaque/human primary brain microvascular endothelial cells. Criteria:
fit: Does the card's measured outcome feed a named step of this programme? 5 = it measures the quantity that step's current practice depends on, on systems the programme uses; 3 = it feeds that step only through a stand-in (another model, system or scale) the programme would have to bridge; 1 = no step of the programme would use the outcome. A step given only in the card's terms, not the programme's own, scores 3 at most.
change: What would the card's outcomes change in this programme's practice? 5 = either outcome changes a choice the programme makes now (what to build, buy, label, check or scale), as its supported practice shows; 3 = only one outcome would change practice, or the change needs further work the card does not do; 1 = neither outcome would change what the programme does. An inactive or archived programme scores 1.
new: Has this programme, or work it relies on, already answered the card's question? 5 = supported claims show its current practice lacks this measurement; 3 = unclear, or partly answered; 1 = already answered. If a checker contradicted the claim that it has not been done, score 3 at most.
Return only JSON: {\"scores\": [{\"programme\": 1, \"criterion\": \"fit | change | new\", \"value\": 1, \"reason\": \"\"}]}"
